The Recipe ¶ gskill consists of two main components: GEPA's optimize_anything -- a powerful API to optimize any textual artifact, including skills . SWE-smith -- a data generation pipeline that creates arbitrary verifiable tasks for any GitHub repository, providing meaningful training and validation data for the optimization process. The gskill pipeline: SWE-smith generates tasks from a target repository, and the GEPA optimization loop iteratively evolves skills through agent evaluation and reflective proposal. Then, the learned skills can be used by any coding agent. Learning skills requires feedback, and feedback requires tasks. This is where SWE-smith comes in. -Agent ¶ To start with, we tested a proof-of-concept implementation of gskill on a simple agent Mini-SWE-Agent with a relatively smaller model, gpt-5-mini. Mini-SWE-Agent performance with GEPA-evolved skills. Skills learned via gskill dramatically improve resolve rates on both repositories. Under 300 rollouts, the Mini-SWE-Agent with GEPA-evolved skills achieves a resolve rate of 82% on Jinja and 93% on Bleve, compared to the baseline of 55% and 24% respectively. While the results are promising, Mini-SWE-Agent is a relatively simple agent, and we are curious to learn if the learned skills are transferable to a production-ready agent. Transfer to Claude Code ¶ To measure whether the learned skills are beneficial for other agents as well, we perform the experiments on the same set of tasks, but with Claude Code. We installed Claude Code into the task environment, and evaluated the performance with and without the learned skills (as a .claude/skills/{repo_name}/SKILL.md file). Here are the results: Claude Code evaluation on Bleve. Skills learned on Mini-SWE-Agent (gpt-5-mini) transfer to Claude Code, boosting pass rates while also reducing average task duration.
